angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 250,452 km at 31.12 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 32.1290 +/- 0.0190 mas (same row, RUWE 1.10): 31.12 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.36 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Díez Alonso et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-239 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018MNRAS.480L...1D/abstract): 250,452 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.4 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Díez Alonso et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-239 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018MNRAS.480L...1D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3420 +/- 18 K from Díez Alonso et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-239 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018MNRAS.480L...1D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Díez Alonso et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-239 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018MNRAS.480L...1D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-239.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.928, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
